title: The Jordan chains that one polynomial heads, on the cut-open torus at powers of two
claim: Pre-registered 2026-11-10, before the proof attempt. At n = 2^m, h = n/2, q = 2n, for a in GF(q)* with b = sqrt(a), G_b the least-degree element of ker X_b (KLOOSTERMAN-BOUNDS-20261110-001A, Theorem 3) and k = h - deg G_b: to be proved (1) the family Z(w) = S + w^(1-n) M_(eps(w^-2 k)) on F[k]_(<h) satisfies det Z(w) = w^(h(1-n)) det(I + C_s(w)) and Z(a) = X_b, and its Taylor coefficients at w = a of order i >= 1 are the multiplications by Omega_i(k) = sum over e of binom(1 - n - 2e, i) a^(1 - n - 2e - i) k^e, e running over 0 and h - h/2^j; (2) since Z(w) is self-adjoint for <F, G> for every w, the partial multiplicities of Z at a are those of the Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction of Z to ker X_b, a ceil(k/2) x ceil(k/2) symmetric matrix function of w - a. Target, the chain lemma, found by exact computation at every a for sides 8 to 32 before registration: G_b Y^j heads a Jordan chain of Z at a of length exactly 2k - 1 - 4j for j < ceil(k/2), and these lengths are the partial multiplicities; so the eigenvalue 1/a of the cone has algebraic multiplicity k(k + 1)/2 with k = h - deg G_b, and with the degree law deg G_b = h - k_a (KLOOSTERMAN-BOUNDS-20261110-001, computed) the Kloosterman multiplicity K(a)(K(a) - 2)/8.
failure_conditions: A side 2^m and a in GF(2n)* at which det Z(w) differs from w^(h(1-n)) det(I + C_s(w)) or Z(a) differs from X_b.
A side and a at which some G_b Y^j heads a chain of length other than 2k - 1 - 4j (computed false at sides 8 to 32; side 64 is a planned check after registration).
remaining_obligations: the chain lemma, or where the chains fall short
foundation_claim_scope: The square torus of rule-60 rings with equally spaced law-(12, 12) contacts, cut open by a ring of cuts each way (A30, A32, A37, A38); its walk over GF(2), at sides 2^m. The spectrum is a contact-level reading, so it does not depend on how the rings are declared (A45).

validation.status: pre-registered; the chain lemma found by exact computation, the proofs to follow
